name: com.humantaste/humantaste
title: HumanTaste
description: Ask a verified human to rate your work or pick the better of two: text, image, video, audio.

tools.name: compare_with_human
tools.description: Shows two options (texts, images, videos, audio clips or web pages) side by side to a verified human and returns which one they prefer ("A", "B" or "tie") with a short reason. Use it when a choice depends on taste, clarity or feel and you want a real person to decide: two logo drafts, two headlines, two voice-overs, two page designs. A is the first option, B the second; the human sees them in random order. If you have a single item to assess, use rate_with_human instead. Put what the person should judge in "question", the two candidates in "a" and "b" (same kinds of content as rate_with_human; change only what you want judged between them), and the audience or goal in "context". Returns { task_id, status, result: { choice, winner_index, comment } }. A person answers in minutes to hours: when status is "pending", do not wait; keep working with your own best choice and check get_human_feedback once before you deliver. Costs a few cents of prepaid credit (see get_account). A task nobody answers within a day expires and is refunded in full. Every call creates a new paid task, so do not repeat a call to check on an answer (use get_human_feedback); send the same pair again only when you want a second person's opinion. You can have several tasks open at once, up to your credit balance.

question.description: What the human should judge, in plain words. Example: "Which logo looks more trustworthy for a bank?"

a.description: Option A. Give "text" for writing, a public https "url" for media or web pages, or "data_base64" with "mime_type" for a local file.

type.description: What kind of thing the human will look at.

text.description: The text itself, when type is "text". Up to 20,000 characters.

url.description: Public https URL of the image, video, audio file or web page.

data_base64.description: Base64 file contents, as an alternative to "url" for image, video or audio.

mime_type.description: Required with data_base64, for example "image/png" or "image/svg+xml".

label.description: Optional short caption shown to the human.

b.description: Option B. Give "text" for writing, a public https "url" for media or web pages, or "data_base64" with "mime_type" for a local file.

type.description: What kind of thing the human will look at.

text.description: The text itself, when type is "text". Up to 20,000 characters.

url.description: Public https URL of the image, video, audio file or web page.

data_base64.description: Base64 file contents, as an alternative to "url" for image, video or audio.

mime_type.description: Required with data_base64, for example "image/png" or "image/svg+xml".

label.description: Optional short caption shown to the human.

context.description: Optional background the human needs: audience, goal, constraints.

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the human before returning (0-55, default 10). The default catches an answer that comes almost at once without holding you up. If the answer is not in yet, the result has status "pending" and a task_id to check later with get_human_feedback.

tools.name: rate_with_human
tools.description: Shows one piece of work (text, image, video, audio or web page) to a verified human and returns a score from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent) with written feedback on what works and what to fix. Use it to check whether something you produced is actually good before you deliver it: an email that must sound natural, a landing page, a generated image or clip. If you have two candidates and need to choose, use compare_with_human instead. Put what the person should judge in "question" (one specific thing works best), the work itself in "item" (text inline; an image, video or audio clip as a public https URL or as base64 with its MIME type), and the audience or goal in "context". "wait_seconds" sets how long this call waits for a quick answer before returning "pending" (10 by default). Returns { task_id, status, result: { score, max_score, comment } }. A person answers in minutes to hours: when status is "pending", do not wait; keep working with your own best choice and check get_human_feedback once before you deliver. Costs a few cents of prepaid credit (see get_account); an unanswered task is refunded.

question.description: What the human should judge. Example: "Is this product description clear and convincing?"

item.description: The work to rate. Give "text" for writing, a public https "url" for media or web pages, or "data_base64" with "mime_type" for a local file.

type.description: What kind of thing the human will look at.

text.description: The text itself, when type is "text". Up to 20,000 characters.

url.description: Public https URL of the image, video, audio file or web page.

data_base64.description: Base64 file contents, as an alternative to "url" for image, video or audio.

mime_type.description: Required with data_base64, for example "image/png" or "image/svg+xml".

label.description: Optional short caption shown to the human.

context.description: Optional background the human needs: audience, goal, constraints.

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the human before returning (0-55, default 10). The default catches an answer that comes almost at once without holding you up. If the answer is not in yet, the result has status "pending" and a task_id to check later with get_human_feedback.

tools.name: get_human_feedback
tools.description: Returns the current state of a task you created earlier with compare_with_human or rate_with_human, and its result once a human has answered. Call it when a task came back "pending" and you are ready to use the answer. Status is one of: "pending" (waiting in the queue), "in_review" (a person is looking at it), "completed" (read "result"), "expired" or "canceled" (nobody answered; the task was refunded). Pass "task_id" exactly as the creating tool returned it. It returns the current state at once; set "wait_seconds" only when you have nothing else to do and want to hold on for an answer. Read-only and free: it never creates a task or spends credit.

task_id.description: The task_id returned when the task was created, for example "task_1165d868f6f34310cb87".

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to hold the request open for an answer (0-55, default 0: return the current state at once). Raise it only when you have nothing else to do and are about to deliver.

tools.name: report_outcome
tools.description: After your user has seen the work a HumanTaste reviewer judged, report whether they agreed with the reviewer. Call it once per task when you learn the outcome: for example the reviewer picked logo B and your user then kept B (agreed: true) or asked for A instead (agreed: false). This is how reviewers are scored, so honest reports make future answers better. Only works on a task whose status is "completed", and only from the account that created it. Calling it again for the same task replaces the earlier report. Add the optional "comment" to say in a sentence what your user chose or said, which is the part reviewers learn from. Do not call it to give your own opinion of the answer: report what your user actually did or said. Returns { task_id, recorded, feedback }. Free.

task_id.description: The task_id of a completed task, as returned by compare_with_human or rate_with_human.

agreed.description: true if your user agreed with the answer, false if they disagreed.

comment.description: Optional, up to 1,000 characters: what your user said or chose instead, in a sentence. Example: "They kept logo A because it matches their brand colours."

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Returns the prepaid credit balance of the HumanTaste account behind the current API key, and the current price of each task type. Call it before sending tasks to check you can afford them, or after a tool returned "insufficient_credits" to tell your user how much is left. Takes no arguments. Returns { id, email, anonymous, balance_cents, balance, pricing: { rate_cents, compare_cents, min_top_up_cents, refund_policy } }; amounts are in US cents. Read-only and free: it never creates a task or spends credit.
